days.title: Lower Reintal Valley Approach
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Olympia Ski Stadium
stops.detail: That becomes apparent shortly after leaving the recently modernised Olympia Ski Stadium in Garmisch-Partenkirchen.

stops.name: Partnachklamm Gorge
stops.detail: In the 700 m long Partnachklamm Gorge, the path boldly snakes its way through rocks, passing within touching distance of rapids, swirling pools and waterfalls.

stops.name: Bockhütte
stops.detail: Ignoring the detour off to the left to the Königshaus at Schachen, so beloved by the Fairy Tale King, it takes another two and half hours before the path reaches the “Bockhütte”.

days.title: Upper Reintal Ascent
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Reintalangerhütte
stops.detail: A waterfall, a little way off the path, heralds the entrance into the Upper Reintal, followed before long by the fluttering of Tibetan prayer flags outside the “Reintalangerhütte”, at 1,369 m.

stops.name: Knorrhütte
stops.detail: Fortunately, refreshments are available at the “Knorrhütte”, with wonderful views of the Wetterstein Mountains on the right.

stops.name: Zugspitzplatt
stops.detail: From here, the path ascends steeply over scree slopes and then the slightly undulating plateau of the rocky glacier known as the Zugspitzplatt.

days.title: Summit Experience and Descent
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Sonnalpin
stops.detail: Upon reaching the “Sonnalpin” restaurant, anyone wishing to avoid the final, most challenging part of the ascent can simply climb into the glacier cable car.

stops.name: Münchner Haus
stops.detail: Crowds of people are teeming around the “Münchner Haus” restaurant.

stops.name: Lake Eibsee
stops.detail: A cable car from Lake Eibsee gets you to the top of Germany’s highest mountain in comfort.
